title: The Wild Thorn
premise: When a mute child arrives at Isandro Pemberton's charm-shop speaking the First Tongue, he discovers she is the vessel of a soul sold to the Court Beneath the Mountain by her own desperate parents—and that his long-vanished hedge-witch mentor was the broker. Hunted by the Crown's witch-finders and shadowed by the Court's debt-collectors, Isandro, the child Wren, and a disgraced witch-finder named Captain Ovelia Thorne must reach the mountain before the thirteenth moon turns. There Isandro learns the truth: his mentor sold her own soul to buy his freedom twelve years ago, and the Court will trade one soul for another. In the end, Isandro refuses the bargain, shatters the contract with the First Tongue itself, and the found family walks out of the mountain carrying a freed soul and an outlawed magic worth more than any law.
about_author: Sebastian Nystrom is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk charms in northern coastal towns before turning to fiction. He writes fantasy about people who keep small promises in large, unforgiving worlds.

chapters.title: The Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. On a rain-lashed night, a mute girl scratches sigils older than any kingdom into his shop door—sigils he recognizes from his apprenticeship. When witch-finders pound on neighboring doors, he hides her among his contraband charms. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into recognition; Isandro realizes the past he fled has found him.

chapters.title: What the Sigils Say
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, with a flashback to his apprenticeship under Mother Vespera. He deciphers enough of Wren's sigils to learn her soul was sold to the Court Beneath the Mountain, and that the broker's mark is Vespera's own. Emotional beat: betrayal and disbelief—the woman who raised him sold a child's soul.

chapters.title: The Witch-Finder's Debt
chapters.summary: Ovelia Thorne's POV. A disgraced witch-finder who once arrested Isandro's kind, Ovelia is ordered to hunt the child—or be tried for her brother's heresy. She tracks them to the shop but hesitates when she sees Wren's sigils match her brother's last writings. Emotional beat: duty cracking against doubt.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, rendered through sensation and image since she cannot speak. The Court's debt-collectors arrive early, wearing borrowed faces, and the shop burns. Isandro, Wren, and Ovelia flee into the sewers with Vespera's old grimoire. Emotional beat: terror becoming resolve; Wren chooses these strangers over her hunters.

chapters.title: The Road Under the Law
chapters.summary: Ovelia's POV. The trio travels disguised as a pilgrim family along the pilgrim road, dodging checkpoints. Ovelia teaches Wren sign-language while Isandro grudgingly teaches Ovelia hedge-craft basics for protection. Emotional beat: wary alliance warming toward trust; three outlaws becoming something like a household.

chapters.title: The Market of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In a border town's hidden magical market, they seek a translator for the grimoire and find instead an old client of Vespera's who reveals the truth: Vespera sold her own soul to buy Isandro's freedom twelve years ago, and Wren's soul is collateral still owed. Emotional beat: guilt detonating—his freedom cost two souls.

chapters.title: Moon Twelve
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The debt-collectors corner them at a river crossing; Ovelia holds the bridge alone so the others can escape, and is taken. Wren, feeling the moon nearly full, begins speaking fragments of the First Tongue aloud—and the river listens. Emotional beat: grief and awe; the child discovers her stolen soul is also a key.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. They descend through the mountain's root-roads into a court of candlelit stone where debts are sung rather than written. Isandro offers himself in exchange for Wren and Vespera, mirroring his mentor's sacrifice. The Court accepts—but Ovelia, brought down in chains, shouts that the contract is forged. Emotional beat: self-sacrifice met with the first crack of hope.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating Isandro's and Wren's POV. As the moon completes its turn above the mountain, Wren speaks the First Tongue fully—not to bargain but to unmake the contract, revealing Vespera's signature was coerced. The Court, bound by its own laws, must release all three souls. Vespera, half-dissolved into the mountain, wakes. Emotional beat: truth overpowering both law and debt.

chapters.title: A Household of Outlaws
chapters.summary: Resolution, Isandro's POV. They emerge changed: Vespera mortal and diminished, Ovelia branded a traitor, Wren speaking softly in two tongues. Magic remains outlawed, justice unwritten—but together they reopen the charm-shop as a sanctuary for the hunted. Emotional beat: quiet joy; loyalty chosen freely, a family made not found.
